releases.name: v3.56.2
releases.body:
### Added

- __CLI authentication:__ Added Vercel AI Gateway and Cline API key provider support for headless CI/automation workflows
- __New model:__ Added Kimi-K2.5 model to Moonshot provider (262K context, image support, prompt caching)
- __Prompt variant:__ Added Trinity Large prompt variant for improved tool-calling support
- __OpenTelemetry:__ Added support for custom headers on metrics and logs endpoints
- __Social links:__ Added community icons (X, Discord, GitHub, Reddit, LinkedIn) to the What's New modal

### Fixed

- __LiteLLM:__ Fixed thinking configuration not appearing for reasoning-capable models
- __OpenTelemetry:__ Fixed endpoint path handling (no longer incorrectly appends `/v1/logs` or `/v1/metrics`) and ensured logs are sent regardless of VSCode telemetry settings
- __CLI auth:__ Fixed `cline auth` displaying incorrect provider information after configuration

### Changed

- __Hooks:__ Hook scripts now run from the workspace repository root instead of filesystem root
- __Default settings:__ Enabled multi-root workspaces, parallel tool calling, and skills by default; disabled strict plan mode by default
- __Settings UI:__ Refreshed feature settings section with collapsible design

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v3.56.1...v3.56.2

### Added

- Native tool calls support for Ollama provider
- Sonnet 4.5 is now the default Amazon Bedrock model id

- Throttle diff view updates during streaming to reduce UI flickering and improve performance.

- Removed Mistral's Devstral-2512 free from the free models list

pulls.title: use cline provider for cline pr review workflow. use npx instead of npm install
pulls.body: This PR will use cline provider for cline pr review workflow. pulls.title: fix(cli): ensure telemetry delivery on shutdown
pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: #XXXX ### Description This PR fixes CLI telemetry undercounting by addressing delivery reliability and event shape consistency. Problem observed: - We launched CLI 2.0 and expected a DAU increase in PostHog, but active user counts remained unexpectedly low compared to install and usage signals. What was happening: - The CLI process had no deterministic telemetry flush path before process exit. - The CLI is often short-lived (especially in non-interactive/piped/command-style usage), which increases the chance that batched PostHog events never get shipped before process termination. - Some interactive callbacks were also exiting directly, which could bypass cleanup in certain flows. - `user.extension_activated` was emitted via a low-level path that skipped the standard metadata enrichment pipeline, making platform-segmented analytics less reliable. Technical approach: - Introduce centralized CLI teardown helpers in `cli/src/index.ts`: - `disposeTelemetryServices()` to flush/close both telemetry and PostHog client resources. - `disposeCliContext()` to run state/controller/error cleanup and telemetry disposal in one place. - Route all CLI shutdown paths through this centralized teardown (plain text mode, interactive cleanup, and signal handling), so telemetry has a chance to flush before process exit. - Keep process exit behavior intact while ensuring cleanup runs first. - Update `TelemetryService.captureExtensionActivated()` to go through `capture(...)` instead of direct provider dispatch so normal metadata is included. Why these choices: - The root issue was not event call sites alone; events were frequently emitted but not reliably delivered. - The safest fix is to guarantee teardown consistency rather than patch individual command paths ad hoc. - Using `capture(...)` for activation aligns this event with every other metadata-enriched event, reducing dashboard/filter mismatch. Alternatives considered: - Emitting more required events (`captureRequired`) to bypass opt-out: rejected, because this would violate expected telemetry controls. - Adding per-command ad hoc delays before exit: rejected, brittle and does not guarantee provider shutdown semantics. - Keeping activation event as-is and only fixing shutdown: rejected, because missing metadata can still undercount platform-segmented dashboards. ### Test Procedure What I validated during implementation: - Confirmed CLI command/event paths in `cli/src/index.ts` and telemetry provider lifecycle in `src/services/telemetry/*`. - Verified published npm artifacts (`cline@2.0.0` and `cline@2.0.5`) include telemetry event capture paths but no explicit CLI telemetry disposal/shutdown path. - Ensured all primary exit paths in CLI now route through centralized cleanup. - Confirmed `captureExtensionActivated` now passes through the metadata-enriched telemetry path. Manual verification recommended after deploy: 1. Run short-lived CLI commands (`cline task "..." --json`, piped stdin flows, quick auth flow). 2. In PostHog, verify increased counts for: - `host.detected` with `name=cline_cli` and `content=initialized` - `user.extension_activated` 3. Validate those events include expected metadata fields (`platform`, `cline_type`, `extension_version`, etc.) for dashboard segmentation. Notes: - I could not run local TypeScript/lint test suites in this worktree because dependencies were not installed (`node_modules` absent in this environment). I can update it immediately if you share the correct issue. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Ensure CLI telemetry delivery by centralizing cleanup and enriching event metadata in `cli/src/index.ts` and `TelemetryService.ts`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Introduce `disposeTelemetryServices()` and `disposeCliContext()` in `cli/src/index.ts` for centralized cleanup of telemetry and CLI context. > - Route all CLI shutdown paths through these functions to ensure telemetry flush before exit. > - Update `captureExtensionActivated()` in `TelemetryService.ts` to use `capture(...)` for metadata enrichment. > - **Functions**: > - Replace direct cleanup calls with `disposeCliContext()` in `runTaskInPlainTextMode()`, `createInkCleanup()`, and other functions in `cli/src/index.ts`. > - Ensure `captureExtensionActivated()` in `initializeCli()` and `runAuth()` uses enriched telemetry path. > - **Misc**: > - Add `telemetryDisposed` flag in `cli/src/index.ts` to prevent redundant disposal calls. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 9dd324f004b7919879af390c394c506b96226a34. pulls.title: fix: restore reasoning behavior parity after #9168
pulls.body:
### Related Issue

Issue: N/A (follow-up to #9168)

### Description

This PR is a targeted behavior-parity follow-up to #9168.

The core goal is not to redesign reasoning controls, but to reduce regression risk by restoring or preserving pre-#9168 runtime behavior where that behavior was relied on, while keeping the post-#9168 configuration model in place.

What problem this PR solves:
- #9168 intentionally centralized reasoning into mode-scoped model config.
- In practice, users reported altered request behavior and settings behavior, especially in OpenAI-compatible paths where deployments vary a lot across proxies and custom gateways.
- We needed a minimal, surgical patch that restores expected defaults and request payload behavior to reduce breakage risk.

Technical approach and why each piece exists:

1) Restore medium fallback as the canonical normalized default
- Updated shared normalization fallback in `src/shared/storage/types.ts` from `low` back to `medium`.
- Updated CLI invalid-flag fallback message/behavior in `cli/src/index.ts` to `medium`.
- Updated UI selector fallback in `webview-ui/src/components/settings/ReasoningEffortSelector.tsx` to `medium`.
- Updated Requesty and OCA provider fallbacks to `medium`.

Why:
- Pre-#9168 behavior and user expectation were centered on medium defaulting.
- Low fallback changed observable behavior for users who never intentionally changed this setting.

2) OpenAI-compatible (`openai.ts`) parity for reasoning-family detection and default send behavior
- Kept the historical reasoning-family model-id detection path:
  - `o1`, `o3`, `o4`, `gpt-5`, excluding `chat` ids.
- In that branch, restored medium-by-default behavior when unset, with explicit `none` still disabling send.

Why:
- OpenAI-compatible is heavily used with custom and proxy backends.
- Users depended on the historical model-id-driven behavior in this provider.

3) Preserve OpenAI Native UX semantics around reasoning picker instead of Anthropic-style thinking budget coupling
- OpenAI Native chat and responses now use reasoning effort semantics directly.
- `none` disables reasoning payload.
- Unset uses normalized medium.

Why:
- In OpenAI Native UI, users get reasoning effort controls, not the Anthropic thinking budget slider.
- Coupling to thinking budget in this provider was inconsistent with UI and caused confusing behavior.

4) Keep gateway transforms explicit and safe for unset values
- In OpenRouter and Vercel transforms, normalization is now only applied when a reasoning effort value is actually set.
- This avoids injecting an implicit effort value simply because normalization function has a default.

Why:
- Avoid surprising payload changes for users who never touched reasoning settings.
- This is especially important in proxy or gateway environments where unknown params can fail hard.

5) Proto cleanup for removed legacy enum value
- Replaced `MINIMAL = 3` with `reserved 3` in `proto/cline/state.proto`.

Why:
- Keeps schema evolution safe and avoids accidental reuse.

6) Unify webview and backend reasoning-support detection logic
- Added shared helper `src/shared/utils/reasoning-support.ts`.
- Backend now re-exports `supportsReasoningEffortForModel` from shared helper.
- Webview provider utility delegates to the same shared helper.

Why:
- Prevents drift where UI says reasoning is supported but backend does not, or vice versa.
- Reduces duplicated, subtly different heuristics.

Debugging journey and non-obvious gotchas:
- During investigation, I compared current behavior directly against pre-#9168 snapshots (`6c53daa88^`) for each provider/transform rather than reasoning from memory.
- The biggest hidden gotcha was that shared normalization defaults can change runtime payload behavior even when a user never set reasoning effort, depending on where normalization is invoked.
- Another subtle issue was provider heterogeneity:
  - OpenAI-compatible often needs conservative behavior because custom stacks vary widely.
  - OpenAI Native is first-party but had a historical coupling to thinking budget that does not match current UI mental model.
- A webview/backend mismatch around reasoning support checks was another source of potentially confusing UX. This PR aligns both sides to one helper.

Alternatives considered:
- Strictly revert all behavior to pre-#9168 in every path.
  - Rejected because it would re-introduce known inconsistencies and keep some buggy coupling in place.
- Keep all #9168 behavior as-is and only add tests.
  - Rejected because users were already seeing altered behavior and needed runtime parity fixes first.

### Test Procedure

Validation executed locally:
- `npm run check-types`
  - Runs proto generation plus type checks for root, webview-ui, and CLI.
- `npm run lint`
  - Runs biome lint plus proto lint checks.

What I verified manually in code and behavior logic:
- Fallback defaults are consistently medium across shared normalization, CLI warning fallback, and reasoning-effort selector fallback.
- OpenAI-compatible reasoning-family branch uses historical model-id parsing and sends medium by default when unset.
- OpenAI Native relies on reasoning effort semantics and respects explicit `none`.
- OpenRouter/Vercel transform logic does not implicitly derive effort from normalization when effort is unset.
- Webview and backend reasoning-support checks call a single shared helper.

Potential break areas reviewed:
- Provider-specific payload construction for reasoning fields.
- Model family detection gates.
- Proto enum backward compatibility safety via reserved slots.

pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: N/A ### Description This PR adds a CLI task flag, `--max-consecutive-mistakes `, so automated runs can control when YOLO mode stops after repeated tool/flow errors. Problem this addresses: Recent Harbor Terminal Bench runs using Gemini via Vercel were repeatedly ending with `Too many consecutive mistakes (3)`. In these runs, the default threshold of 3 was terminating many trials before the model could recover. We already fixed other major run configuration problems (model routing, prompt delimiter handling, timeout), but this specific threshold remained hardcoded from a CLI operator perspective. That meant we could not isolate model quality from safety-stop sensitivity without code changes. Why this change is needed: The core task engine already supports configurable `maxConsecutiveMistakes` in global state, but current CLI options do not expose that setting for task execution. As a result, benchmark runners and CI wrappers cannot tune this value at invocation time. This PR closes that gap by exposing a first-class flag and applying it during task option setup. Technical approach: - Added a new CLI option on both task entry surfaces: - `cline task ... --max-consecutive-mistakes ` - `cline ... --max-consecutive-mistakes ` - Extended task option parsing to include `maxConsecutiveMistakes`. - Added normalization and validation logic: - accepts integer values >= 1 - invalid values produce a warning and are ignored - When valid, writes `maxConsecutiveMistakes` into state before task execution and emits a telemetry host event. Debugging journey and non-obvious gotchas: During investigation, there was an assumption that this might already be externally configurable through historical syntax (`-s max_consecutive_mistakes=...`). That path appears in older/deprecated CLI docs and comments, but does not exist in the current `commander`-based CLI command parser. The key gotcha is that configurability existed in core state and internal flows, yet was not surfaced by current public CLI flags. This made run-time tuning look available in theory while still unavailable in practice. Decisions and alternatives considered: I considered bypassing the mistake limit entirely in YOLO mode for benchmark runs, but rejected that because it weakens protection globally and risks runaway loops in normal automation usage. Exposing a threshold knob is safer and more flexible: - default behavior remains unchanged at 3 - benchmark operators can explicitly raise the limit - regular users keep existing safeguards unless they opt in How to test: 1. Parser-level tests (already added) verify the new option is accepted in both command forms. 2. Run `cline task "echo test" --max-consecutive-mistakes 10` and confirm no parse errors. 3. Run with an invalid value (for example `0` or `abc`) and confirm warning is emitted and execution continues with existing configured/default limit. 4. In benchmark wrappers, append `--max-consecutive-mistakes 999` to confirm YOLO stops are no longer dominated by the threshold in early recovery scenarios. ### Test Procedure I validated this change with focused CLI tests and static checks: - `npm -C cli run test:run -- src/index.test.ts` - `npm -C cli run typecheck` I also added explicit parser tests for: - task command form parsing (`--max-consecutive-mistakes 999`) - default command form parsing (`--max-consecutive-mistakes 7`) Potential break surface considered: - Existing invocations are unaffected because the new flag is optional. - Invalid values are handled defensively with warning + no state write. - Default threshold behavior remains unchanged when the flag is omitted. ### Type of Change - pulls.body:
# Add bundled endpoints support for enterprise deployments

## Summary

This PR adds support for bundling custom `endpoints.json` files directly into Cline distribution packages (VSIX and CLI tarball). This enables enterprise customers to distribute pre-configured Cline installations that automatically connect to their self-hosted infrastructure without requiring manual configuration.

## Problem

Enterprise customers using self-hosted Cline deployments currently need to manually create `~/.cline/endpoints.json` files on each installation. This creates friction in enterprise rollouts and increases support burden.

## Solution

Cline now checks for bundled `endpoints.json` in the package installation directory before checking the user directory:

1. **Priority order**: `<installation-dir>/endpoints.json` → `~/.cline/endpoints.json` → standard mode
2. **Automatic detection**: When found, Cline automatically switches to self-hosted mode
3. **Auto-update protection**: CLI auto-update is disabled for bundled enterprise packages to preserve configuration
4. **Clear logging**: Logs "Cline running in self-hosted mode with custom endpoints"
33a35
5. Auto-update is automatically disabled for bundled packages to preserve enterprise configuration

## How It Works

### For VS Code Extension

1. Build standard VSIX: `npx @vscode/vsce package`
2. Bundle endpoints: `./scripts/add-endpoints-to-vsix.sh input.vsix output.vsix endpoints.json`
3. Distribute the bundled VSIX to users
5. On installation, extension finds and loads the bundled `endpoints.json`

### For CLI

1. Build standard tarball: `npm pack`
2. Bundle endpoints: `./scripts/add-endpoints-to-npm.sh input.tgz output.tgz endpoints.json`
3. Distribute the bundled tarball to users
4. On installation, CLI finds and loads the bundled `endpoints.json`

## Key Changes

### Core Implementation

- **`src/config.ts`**: Updated `ClineEndpoint.initialize()` to check bundled location first; added `isBundledConfig()` method to detect bundled enterprise packages
- **`cli/src/utils/update.ts`**: Updated `autoUpdateOnStartup()` to skip auto-update for bundled enterprise packages
- **`cli/src/index.ts`**: Moved auto-update call to run after endpoints initialization; fixed Logger subscription order to capture initialization logs- **`cli/src/vscode-context.ts`**: Fixed ES module path resolution for CLI

### Packaging Scripts

- **`scripts/add-endpoints-to-vsix.sh`**: Bundle endpoints into VSIX
- **`scripts/add-endpoints-to-npm.sh`**: Bundle endpoints into CLI tarball
- **`scripts/add-endpoints-to-jetbrains.sh`**: Bundle endpoints into JetBrains ZIP
- **`scripts/test-bundled-endpoints.sh`**: Complete build and test workflow

### Documentation

- **`docs/enterprise-solutions/bundled-endpoints.mdx`**: Complete enterprise guide
- **`.changeset/big-turkeys-shake.md`**: Patch changeset entry

## Testing

### Automated Test

```bash
./scripts/test-bundled-endpoints.sh
```

This builds both VSIX and CLI packages with bundled staging endpoints and verifies:
- Packages contain `endpoints.json`
- Files are in correct locations
- JSON structure is valid

### Manual Testing

**VS Code Extension:**
```bash
code --install-extension ./dist-bundled/claude-dev-3.56.2-with-endpoints.vsix
# Open Output > Cline, verify: "LOG Cline running in self-hosted mode with custom endpoints"
```

**CLI:**
```bash
npm install -g ./dist-bundled/cline-2.0.3-with-endpoints.tgz
cline config
cat ~/.cline/data/logs/cline-cli.1.log
# Verify: "LOG Cline running in self-hosted mode with custom endpoints"
```

## Deployment Workflow

1. Build official release packages as normal
2. Use packaging scripts to bundle custom endpoints
3. Distribute bundled packages to enterprise users
4. Users install and automatically connect to self-hosted infrastructure

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a backward-compatible addition:
- Existing installations without bundled endpoints work unchanged
- User `~/.cline/endpoints.json` files still work and are checked as fallback
- Standard (non-enterprise) installations are unaffected

## Important Notes

### Auto-Update Protection for Enterprise Packages

The CLI now includes intelligent auto-update protection:
- **Bundled enterprise packages**: Auto-update is automatically disabled to prevent overwriting custom configuration
- **User `~/.cline/endpoints.json`**: Auto-update remains enabled (users can manage updates themselves)
- **Standard installations**: Auto-update works normally
- **Manual override**: Set `CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` environment variable to disable auto-update in any scenario

This ensures enterprise customers' bundled packages remain stable and don't get silently replaced with standard npm versions.

## Checklist

- [x] Code changes implemented and tested
- [x] Documentation added
- [x] Changeset created
- [x] Both VS Code extension and CLI verified working
- [x] Packaging scripts tested
- [x] No breaking changes

pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: N/A ### Description This PR fixes a model selection bug in the Vercel AI Gateway provider that can silently route requests to the wrong model. Problem statement: - In Harbor benchmark runs, we configured trials with `vercel:google/gemini-3-pro-preview`. - At runtime, many trial artifacts (`prompt_manifest.latest.json`) reported `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`. - This produced misleading benchmark conclusions because the configured model and the effective model diverged. Root cause: - `VercelAIGatewayHandler.getModel()` only returned the configured model when both `openRouterModelId` and `openRouterModelInfo` were present. - If model info was missing, the method fell back to `openRouterDefaultModelId`, which is currently `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`. - That fallback changed the actual model identity, not only metadata. Why this happened in practice: - The configuration path can set a provider model ID even when per-model metadata is unavailable or not hydrated. - In that state, using a default model ID is dangerous because it changes model behavior rather than preserving intent. Technical approach in this PR: - Updated `VercelAIGatewayHandler.getModel()` to match the already-correct behavior in `ClineHandler.getModel()`. - New behavior: 1. If `modelId` and `modelInfo` exist, return both. 2. If only `modelId` exists, preserve that ID and use `openRouterDefaultModelInfo` as metadata. 3. If no `modelId` exists, use default ID and default info. Why this is the right tradeoff: - Preserving the configured model ID prevents silent model swaps. - Falling back only metadata is safer than falling back model identity. - This keeps runtime behavior aligned with user or evaluator intent even when metadata is incomplete. Debugging journey and validation context: - We started from benchmark anomalies where Gemini-labeled runs showed unexpectedly Claude-like outcomes. - We compared `config.json` model settings with runtime prompt manifests in trial artifacts. - We consistently observed configured Gemini plus runtime Sonnet in affected Vercel runs. - We then traced model resolution from provider config to `buildApiHandler()` to `VercelAIGatewayHandler.getModel()`. - We found the strict `modelId && modelInfo` guard causing default-model fallback. - We verified that `ClineHandler` already contained the safer fallback and mirrored that pattern here. Alternatives considered: - Fail hard when `modelInfo` is missing. - Rejected because this would turn recoverable config states into hard execution failures. - Hydrate model metadata eagerly in every auth or config path before task start. - Useful follow-up, but larger surface area and not required to fix incorrect model routing. - Keep existing fallback to default model. - Rejected because it silently violates configured model selection. Non-obvious gotcha discovered: - A fallback that seems like a metadata default can become a model routing default if `id` and `info` are coupled in one condition. - This is especially risky in benchmark pipelines where model identity is the primary controlled variable. ### Test Procedure What I ran locally: 1. `npm ci` 2. `npm run protos` 3. `npm run test:unit -- src/core/api/providers/__tests__/vercel-ai-gateway.test.ts` What was verified: - New unit tests validate all three getModel branches: - configured id and info - configured id without info - missing id - Existing unit suite invoked in this run stayed green in this environment. - Mocha summary from the run: `865 passing`, `4 pending`. Risk assessment: - Low risk, narrow scope. - Behavior only changes when `modelInfo` is missing. - Normal path with both id and info remains unchanged. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots N/A. This is a backend provider selection fix. ### Additional Notes This fix intentionally aligns Vercel AI Gateway model fallback behavior with the existing Cline provider behavior to keep model identity stable under partial metadata conditions. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes model selection in `VercelAIGatewayHandler` to preserve configured model ID when metadata is missing, preventing silent model swaps. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes model selection in `VercelAIGatewayHandler.getModel()` to preserve configured model ID when metadata is missing. > - Aligns behavior with `ClineHandler.getModel()` to prevent silent model swaps. > - **Tests**: > - Adds `vercel-ai-gateway.test.ts` to test `getModel()` for cases with both model ID and info, only model ID, and missing model ID. > - **Misc**: > - Updates `getModel()` in `vercel-ai-gateway.ts` to use default metadata when only model ID is present. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for e7fc7a788870dc9032c2158161cafa0bafc20d60. pulls.title: feat: add double-check completion experimental feature
pulls.body: ### Related Issue Internal -- motivated by Harbor Terminal Bench 2.0 results analysis. ### Description One of the biggest failure patterns we've seen in Harbor Terminal Bench 2.0 runs is premature `attempt_completion`. The model declares the task done before all required work is actually finished -- files not created, steps skipped, edge cases ignored. We initially discussed heuristic approaches (inferring required output files from the task description), but that felt too non-deterministic and fragile. This PR takes a deterministic approach instead: a two-step completion flow. When enabled, the first `attempt_completion` call in a task is rejected with a tool error that asks the model to re-verify its work against the original task. The rejection message includes the initial task text (up to 4000 chars) so the model has concrete context to check against, not just a generic "did you finish?" prompt. The second `attempt_completion` call proceeds normally. The mechanics are simple: a `completionAttemptCount` counter on `TaskState` increments on every `attempt_completion` call. When the setting is enabled and the count is 1, the handler returns early with a `formatResponse.toolError(...)` before any hooks or UI logic run. The counter resets naturally per-task since `TaskState` is created fresh for each task. `consecutiveMistakeCount` is intentionally NOT incremented on rejection since this is expected behavior, not a mistake. The setting (`doubleCheckCompletionEnabled`, default `false`) flows through the full stack following the same pattern as `yoloModeToggled` and `strictPlanModeEnabled`: proto field in `UpdateSettingsRequest` (field 41) and auto-generated `Settings` message (field 176), `USER_SETTINGS_FIELDS` in `state-keys.ts`, `TaskConfig` interface + `TASK_CONFIG_KEYS` + `ToolExecutor.asToolConfig()` wiring, `ExtensionState`, `getStateToPostToWebview()`, and `updateSettings()` handler. How to enable: - VS Code extension: Settings > Features > Experimental > "Double-Check Completion" toggle - CLI flag: `cline --double-check-completion "your task"` - CLI TUI: Settings panel > Features > "Double-check completion" toggle Also adds a `cli:run` convenience script (`npm run cli:run`) for quick CLI testing without needing to type `node cli/dist/cli.mjs`. ### Test Procedure - All three TypeScript targets (extension, webview, CLI) pass `tsc --noEmit` with zero errors - Full unit test suite passes: 858 passing, 0 failing - 9 new unit tests covering: disabled path (no rejection), enabled first call rejected, enabled second call accepted, third+ calls accepted, `consecutiveMistakeCount` not affected by rejection, counter initialization at 0, counter reset with new TaskState - Default is `false` everywhere, so existing users see zero behavior change unless they explicitly opt in ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Additional Notes Files changed (15): | Layer | Files | |-------|-------| | Proto/state | `proto/cline/state.proto`, `src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts`, `src/shared/ExtensionMessage.ts` | | Controller | `src/core/controller/state/updateSettings.ts`, `src/core/controller/index.ts` | | Task core | `src/core/task/TaskState.ts`, `src/core/task/ToolExecutor.ts`, `src/core/task/tools/handlers/AttemptCompletionHandler.ts` | | TaskConfig | `src/core/task/tools/types/TaskConfig.ts`, `src/core/task/tools/utils/ToolConstants.ts` | | Webview | `webview-ui/src/.../FeatureSettingsSection.tsx`, `webview-ui/src/.../ExtensionStateContext.tsx` | | CLI | `cli/src/index.ts`, `cli/src/components/SettingsPanelContent.tsx` | | Tests | `src/core/task/tools/handlers/__tests__/AttemptCompletionHandler.doubleCheck.test.ts` | ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Add `doubleCheckCompletionEnabled` feature to require task re-verification before final completion, with CLI support and tests. > > - pulls.title: fix(prompt): add output precision and threshold iteration rules
pulls.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** Part of Terminal-Bench hillclimb effort (follows #9154, #9156, #9159, #9161) ### Description Adds two concise, general-purpose prompt rules to improve agent output quality, tested and validated via Terminal-Bench benchmarks on Harbor. **Rule 1 — Output precision:** "When writing output files, produce exactly what the task specifies—no extra columns, fields, debug output, or commentary. Match the requested format precisely." **Rule 2 — Threshold iteration:** "When the task specifies numerical thresholds or accuracy targets, verify your result meets the criteria before completing. If close but not passing, iterate rather than declaring completion." These rules address two common failure patterns: - Agent adds extra columns/debug output to files (e.g., adding an `instance` column to a CSV that should only have `period,severity,count`) - Agent declares completion without verifying numerical results meet stated thresholds (e.g., Tm difference of 5.44°C when ≤5.0 was required) **What was excluded and why:** A third "no-cleanup" rule was tested and deliberately dropped. Despite using "STRICTLY FORBIDDEN" language, it failed to prevent the agent from deleting deployed content on `configure-git-webserver`, and caused a side-effect on `polyglot-c-py` (prevented legitimate build artifact cleanup). The cleanup behavior is too deeply trained to override via prompt rules. ### Test Procedure Tested on [Harbor](https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor) Terminal-Bench benchmark with Opus 4.6 (job `2026-02-07__16-15-00`, 6 targeted tasks on Modal): | Task | Baseline | With Rules | Rule | |------|----------|-----------|------| | log-summary-date-ranges | ❌ 0.0 | ✅ **1.0** | output precision | | dna-insert | ❌ 0.0 | ✅ **1.0** | threshold iteration | | mteb-leaderboard | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (context overflow — not a prompt issue) | | polyglot-c-py | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (build artifacts — tested no-cleanup, excluded) | | configure-git-webserver | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (self-sabotage — no-cleanup rule failed) | | train-fasttext | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (8% accuracy gap too large to iterate past) | **2 clear FAIL→PASS flips** from 4 insertions across 2 files. No regressions expected — both rules constrain behavior toward correctness. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Additional Notes These two rules follow [Cursor's agent best practices](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-best-practices): "Add rules only when you notice the agent making the same mistake repeatedly. Keep rules focused on essentials." Both are concise (1 line each), general-purpose, and empirically validated. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds rules for output precision and threshold iteration to improve agent output quality in multiple snapshot and template files. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds rule for output precision: "Produce exactly what the task specifies—no extra columns, fields, debug output, or commentary. Match the requested format precisely." > - Adds rule for threshold iteration: "Verify numerical thresholds or accuracy targets before completing. If close but not passing, iterate rather than declaring completion." > - **Files**: > - Updates `rules.ts` and `template.ts` to include new rules in the rules template. > - Adds new rules to `anthropic_claude_sonnet_4-basic.snap`, `cline_devstral-basic.snap`, and `openai_gpt_3-basic.snap` among others. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for e57b64654a976774f45557ede8ee6c5369c1998a. pulls.title: fix(cli): route PostHog networking through shared fetch
pulls.body:
### Related Issue

Issue: N/A

### Description

This PR fixes a CLI networking inconsistency that surfaced as noisy terminal errors when telemetry flushes failed in corporate proxy environments.

Problem observed:
- A CLI user hit repeated `Connection error` retries during PostHog flush.
- The root error chain included `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` from Node TLS.
- The output looked like a CLI failure even though it was telemetry flush behavior.

What was actually broken:
- Cline already has a shared network layer in `src/shared/net.ts` that standardizes proxy handling and certificate behavior for standalone/CLI.
- PostHog clients were not using that shared fetch path. They were relying on default SDK/Node fetch behavior.
- That creates a split-brain networking setup where model/provider traffic and telemetry traffic can behave differently under the same environment.

Technical approach:
- Inject Cline's shared fetch into every PostHog client constructor, so telemetry/error/feature-flag traffic follows the same network path as other CLI requests.
- Kept changes minimal and scoped only to PostHog initialization sites.

Files changed:
- `src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogClientProvider.ts`
- `src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogTelemetryProvider.ts`
- `src/services/error/providers/PostHogErrorProvider.ts`
- `src/services/feature-flags/providers/PostHogFeatureFlagsProvider.ts`

Each now passes:
- `fetch: (url, options) => fetch(url, options as RequestInit)`

Debugging journey and non-obvious findings:
- At first glance this looked like CLI command failure.
- Tracing shutdown paths showed Cline does catch/contain most provider disposal errors, but PostHog core itself logs flush failures to stderr on network failure, which makes the issue very visible.
- I validated that the noisy retry/error text is from PostHog SDK internals, not from Cline's Logger.
- I also checked whether Cline had existing fallback logic for this specific PostHog error signature and found none.
- The strongest fix available within Cline was to remove the network-stack mismatch by using shared fetch in PostHog constructors.

Alternatives considered:
- Disable PostHog retries/logging globally: would require deeper SDK behavior changes and would reduce useful diagnostics.
- Silence stderr around shutdown: risky because it can hide unrelated runtime errors.
- Only document `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`: helpful but not sufficient when the app itself uses two different fetch paths.

Why this approach:
- Aligns telemetry networking with existing Cline architecture.
- Minimal blast radius.
- Improves behavior specifically in CLI/standalone proxy and custom CA setups.

### Test Procedure

What I tested:
1. Ran formatting/lint checks on all touched files.
2. Reviewed final diff to confirm only PostHog constructor options were changed, plus import ordering/type-only import cleanups from formatter.
3. Confirmed no unrelated files were modified.

Commands run:
- `npx biome check --write src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogClientProvider.ts src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogTelemetryProvider.ts src/services/error/providers/PostHogErrorProvider.ts src/services/feature-flags/providers/PostHogFeatureFlagsProvider.ts`
- `npx biome check --diagnostic-level=error src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogClientProvider.ts src/services/telemetry/providers/posthog/PostHogTelemetryProvider.ts src/services/error/providers/PostHogErrorProvider.ts src/services/feature-flags/providers/PostHogFeatureFlagsProvider.ts`

Current confidence and limits:
- High confidence in the code-level fix because it is a narrow constructor option injection across all PostHog entry points.
- Full repository `tsc` currently fails in this worktree due pre-existing generated proto/module resolution issues unrelated to this PR, so I did targeted validation on touched files.

Potential impact checked:
- Telemetry provider path
- Error provider path
- Feature flags provider path
- Shared PostHog client provider path

### Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Pre-flight Checklist

### Screenshots

### Additional Notes

Operational guidance for affected users still applies:
- Set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to corporate CA PEM when TLS interception is in place.
- Ensure proxy env vars (`https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, `no_proxy`) are correctly configured.

This PR focuses on making PostHog traffic honor the same shared network behavior as the rest of CLI traffic.

pulls.body: ### Related Issue Extends #9168 (reasoning effort model config) ### Description The `--thinking` CLI flag previously only toggled extended thinking on/off with a hardcoded 1024 token budget. This change makes it accept an optional number so users can set whatever budget they want. #### New commands this unlocks ```bash # Before: only boolean toggle (always 1024 tokens) cline "prompt" --thinking # After: optional custom budget cline "prompt" --thinking # 1024 tokens (default, same as before) cline "prompt" --thinking 4096 # 4096 tokens cline "prompt" --thinking 8000 # 8000 tokens ``` Invalid values (negative numbers, non-numeric strings) get a warning and fall back to 1024. #### Context on budget sizing The webview settings UI caps the thinking budget slider at 6000 tokens. You're unlikely to see meaningful benefit going much higher than that for most tasks, but the CLI doesn't enforce a cap -- if you want to experiment with larger budgets, you can. The budget is applied to both plan and act modes (synced when separate models is disabled, which is the default). #### Changes - `cli/src/index.ts`: Changed `--thinking` option from boolean to `[tokens]` (optional argument). pulls.body:
### Related Issue

Issue: N/A

### Description

## Summary

This PR changes reasoning effort from a global setting into model configuration scoped by mode:

- `planModeReasoningEffort`
- `actModeReasoningEffort`

It updates all affected layers:

- storage and proto conversion
- controller update paths
- provider request construction
- webview settings UI
- CLI and TUI UX

It also removes duplicate model selection UX under the chat input and routes model selection through settings.

## Goals

1. Make reasoning effort mode specific (Plan and Act can differ).
2. Use one reasoning effort concept for GPT and Gemini families where applicable.
3. Keep provider specific mapping in provider/request code.
4. Keep UI behavior consistent across settings surfaces.
5. Prevent request payload conflicts such as sending incompatible reasoning fields together.

## What changed by layer

### 1) Types, storage, proto conversion

- Added canonical reasoning effort values in shared storage types.
- Added mode-scoped reasoning effort fields in API config flow.
- Updated proto conversion and controller update paths to carry these values end to end.

Key files:

pulls.title: fix(prompt): guide models to use -- for leading-dash positional args
pulls.body: Problem One TerminalBench failure mode is command construction where positional text that begins with `-` can be interpreted as CLI options by downstream tools unless `--` is used to end option parsing. In practice, this can cause hard failures before real task progress if an argument is intended to be data but gets parsed as a flag. This PR takes the prompt-first approach requested for this track. Instead of changing parser behavior in CLI runtime code, it adds explicit guidance to the system prompt to insert `--` before positional values when those values may start with `-`. What changed - Added one rule line in the shared rules component: - /Users/saoud/.codex/worktrees/1bd6/cline/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/components/rules.ts - Added the equivalent rule in next-gen variant template so behavior is explicit for that path: - /Users/saoud/.codex/worktrees/1bd6/cline/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/variants/next-gen/template.ts - Added the equivalent rule in gemini-3 overrides to keep variant parity: - /Users/saoud/.codex/worktrees/1bd6/cline/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/variants/gemini-3/overrides.ts Rule text added When passing untrusted or variable text as positional command arguments, insert `--` before the positional values if they may begin with `-` (for example `my-cli -- "$value"`). This prevents the values from being parsed as options. Why this should help TerminalBench - Some benchmark trajectories fail on command invocation shape and never reach meaningful task execution. - This rule nudges model output to a safer shell pattern that avoids option parsing collisions. - It is a low-risk behavioral guidance change with no runtime execution-path changes. Debugging and decision notes - I previously prototyped a runtime CLI parser normalization approach, then discarded it on request to keep this as a prompt-only solution. - I validated that snapshot changes are exactly the expected prompt-line insertions across the affected model families. - Keeping this as prompt-only preserves strict CLI parser semantics while still improving model command hygiene. Risks and tradeoffs - This does not harden parser behavior for non-model invocations (for example, direct manual CLI usage that omits `--`). - This relies on model compliance. It should reduce incidence, but not guarantee elimination. - If later data shows residual failures, the next step would be runtime parser hardening as a separate PR. ### Test Procedure 1. pulls.title: fix(terminal): surface command exit codes in results
pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: N/A ### Description This is PR 2 in the TerminalBench score recovery sequence. In Harbor TerminalBench failures, we saw cases where command execution looked successful in the assistant-facing summary even when the underlying process exited non-zero. That makes the agent overconfident and increases premature completion risk. The main issue was that orchestration returned a generic "Command executed" message on completion without carrying explicit exit status through the terminal process contract. This PR makes command completion status explicit and consistent end to end. What changed: - Added terminal completion metadata (`exitCode`, `signal`) to the shared terminal process event contract. - Propagated completion metadata from standalone child process close events. - Propagated completion metadata from VSCode shell integration output by parsing `]633;D;` markers when available. - Updated command orchestration result text to distinguish: - `Command executed successfully (exit code 0).` - `Command failed with exit code N.` - `Command terminated by signal X.` - Updated standalone background command tracking to mark non-zero exit/signal as error and persist exit details. Why this should improve TerminalBench: - Strict benchmark tasks often depend on correctly handling failed compile/test/script steps. - The model now gets direct, structured failure signals instead of ambiguous success phrasing. - This should reduce false-positive progress and improve retry/fix loops. pulls.title: fix: use vscode.env.asExternalUri for auth callback URLs in VS Code Web
pulls.body: ## Summary Follow-up to #9111. Fixes the remaining callback redirect issue from #5109. After PR #9111 fixed opening the sign-in page in remote environments, users reported that the OAuth **callback redirect** still didn't work in VS Code Web (`code serve-web`). After authenticating, the browser would redirect to `vscode://saoudrizwan.claude-dev/auth` which opens the **local desktop VS Code app** instead of routing back to the web instance. ## Root Cause `getCallbackUrl()` in `extension.ts` and `getIdeRedirectUri()` were constructing raw `vscode://` URIs: ```typescript // Old: const getCallbackUrl = async () => `${vscode.env.uriScheme}://${context.extension.id}` ``` In VS Code Web, this `vscode://` scheme is handled by the OS, which opens the desktop app. ## Fix Wrap both functions with [`vscode.env.asExternalUri()`](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#env.asExternalUri) which resolves URIs appropriately for the current environment: | Environment | Input | Behavior | |---|---|---| | VS Code Desktop | `vscode://saoudrizwan.claude-dev` | Returns unchanged | | VS Code Remote SSH | `vscode://saoudrizwan.claude-dev` | Adds remote authority for proper routing | | VS Code Web (`code serve-web`) | `vscode://saoudrizwan.claude-dev` | Transforms to HTTPS URL that routes through the web server | ## Changes - `src/extension.ts`: `getCallbackUrl()` now uses `vscode.env.asExternalUri()` - `src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/getIdeRedirectUri.ts`: Also uses `asExternalUri()` ## Testing Notes - ⚠️ **Desktop VS Code**: Should be a no-op - verify auth still works normally - ⚠️ **Remote SSH**: Verify auth callback still routes correctly - 🎯 **VS Code Web**: Callback should now redirect back to the web instance ## Related - #5109 - Original issue - #9111 - Previous fix (openExternal) - #2152 - "Cline cannot be signed in when using vscode web" - cline/intellij-plugin#735 - IntelliJ fix for openExternal ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes OAuth callback redirect in VS Code Web using `vscode.env.asExternalUri()` and adds a fallback for `openExternal` in JetBrains environments. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes OAuth callback redirect in VS Code Web by using `vscode.env.asExternalUri()` in `getCallbackUrl()` in `src/extension.ts` and `getIdeRedirectUri()` in `src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/getIdeRedirectUri.ts`. > - In VS Code Web, transforms `vscode://` URIs to HTTPS URLs for proper routing. > - In VS Code Desktop and Remote SSH, URIs remain unchanged or are adjusted for remote authority. > - **Fallback Mechanism**: > - Adds fallback for `openExternal` in `src/utils/env.ts` to use the `open` npm package if the host doesn't support the RPC, specifically for JetBrains. > - **Misc**: > - Minor refactor in `src/extension.ts` to handle `vscode.env.uiKind` checks for web environments. > - Updates to `openExternal` function to log errors and show messages if URL opening fails. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for e34724572de0b3e131e0633345a8a42597f1eb5d. pulls.title: fix(prompt): require verification before completion
pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: N/A ### Description This is PR 1 in the TerminalBench recovery plan. In our recent Harbor TerminalBench run (89 trials, 51 pass, 37 fail, 1 verifier timeout), a repeated failure mode was early or incorrect completion when outputs were not explicitly verified. The key prompt rule that contributed to this was the instruction telling the agent to assume terminal success when expected output is missing. In strict verifier tasks this is dangerous, because missing output often means the task is still failing, not that output streaming is delayed. I changed the core prompt text to push the model toward verification-first behavior. Instead of assuming success, the prompt now tells the model to treat missing or incomplete output as unverified and run follow-up checks before moving on. I also updated the objective section so attempt_completion is explicitly gated on verification of required files, required format/content constraints, and absence of forbidden artifacts. Why this should help TerminalBench specifically: - Several failing tasks were artifact and format strict, where premature completion caused direct verifier failures - This change nudges the model to run lightweight checks before finalizing - It is low-risk compared to runtime/tool contract changes because this PR only updates prompt instructions Files changed: - `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/components/rules.ts` - `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/variants/next-gen/template.ts` - `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/components/objective.ts` - Snapshot baselines under `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/__tests__/__snapshots__/` updated to match new prompt output Debugging and decision notes: - I first ran prompt integration tests without snapshot updates to confirm changes were isolated to expected snapshot mismatches - The mismatches were exactly in the sections touched by this PR - After confirming scope, I regenerated snapshots and re-ran tests to green - I intentionally kept this PR text-only and did not include runtime enforcement yet so behavior change can be reviewed in isolation Alternatives considered: - Adding a hard runtime completion gate in this PR - I skipped that here because it is a bigger behavior change and is better handled in a follow-up PR once prompt-only impact is evaluated ### Test Procedure I validated this in two phases: 1. Scope check before snapshot refresh - `npm run test:unit -- src/core/prompts/system-prompt/__tests__/integration.test.ts` - Expected result: snapshot mismatches only in prompt outputs affected by the new rules/objective text 2. Final validation after snapshot refresh - `npm run test:unit -- src/core/prompts/system-prompt/__tests__/integration.test.ts --update-snapshots` - Result: passing (`849 passing`, `4 pending`) What could break: - Prompt behavior may become slightly more conservative in situations where terminal output is intermittently missing - This is intentional for benchmark correctness, and follow-up PRs will tune runtime signaling and timeout behavior to reduce false negatives ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots Not applicable for this backend/prompt change. ### Additional Notes Planned next PRs in this TerminalBench series: 1. Surface non-zero exit codes clearly in terminal tool results 2. Tune command timeout strategy for long-running tasks 3. Fix CLI leading-dash prompt parsing edge case ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > This PR updates prompt instructions to require verification before task completion, addressing issues in TerminalBench by modifying rules and objectives to ensure tasks are verified before marking them as complete, with corresponding snapshot updates. > > - **Behavior**: > - Updates prompt instructions in `rules.ts` and `objective.ts` to require verification of task completion before using `attempt_completion`. > - Modifies rules to treat missing or incomplete output as unverified, requiring follow-up checks. > - **Files**: > - Changes in `rules.ts` and `objective.ts` to update task verification logic. > - Snapshot updates in `__snapshots__` to align with new prompt behavior. > - **Testing**: > - Validated changes with prompt integration tests, ensuring snapshot mismatches were expected and isolated to modified sections. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 927620bddff5e13b0f44908cb68b0301f982b7b0. pulls.title: chore(ci): add reviewer source footer to PR bot comments
pulls.body: ### Related Issue Issue: N/A ### Description This PR makes the two automated PR reviewers visibly identifiable in their final comment output. Problem this solves: When both review automations are enabled on the same PR, maintainers and contributors can see two long review comments but it is not always obvious at a glance which workflow generated which one. What changed: - Updated `/Users/saoud/.codex/worktrees/e576/cline/.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml` prompt instructions so Claude must append a final footer block: - `---` - `Generated by Claude PR Review` - Updated `/Users/saoud/.codex/worktrees/e576/cline/.github/workflows/cline-pr-review.yml` prompt instructions so Cline must append a final footer block: - `---` - `Generated by Cline PR Code Review` Technical approach: I only changed prompt instructions inside each workflow, near the existing `Post your review` section. I did not change triggers, permissions, runtime setup, secrets, labels, or any command execution logic. Debugging journey and context: - We first investigated why Claude review was not running while Cline was. - I validated workflow configs in-repo and found no job-level disable condition besides skipping drafts. - I then checked GitHub Actions workflow state using `gh workflow list --all` and confirmed root cause: `Claude PR Review` was `disabled_manually` while `Cline PR Code Review` was active. - We re-enabled `Claude PR Review` with `gh workflow enable "Claude PR Review"` and verified it is active. - After that, we added these source footers so future dual-review runs are easy to distinguish. Non-obvious gotchas discovered: - Workflow YAML being present in the repo does not mean it is enabled in GitHub Actions. - This repo had a real split state where one review workflow was active and the other was manually disabled. - Prompt-only edits are low-risk, but they still rely on model instruction-following, so the footer is expected strongly but not cryptographically enforced. Decisions made and alternatives considered: - Chosen: add explicit footer instructions in both prompts. This is simple, low-risk, and keeps both workflows independent. - Considered: changing comment body assembly through shell-generated fixed suffix. Rejected for now because it is more invasive and would require restructuring how each bot posts its final message. - Considered: labels-only distinction. Rejected because labels are less discoverable than a visible footer in the review comment itself. ### Test Procedure I validated the following: 1. Confirmed both workflow files contain the new footer directives at the prompt level. 2. Confirmed only these two workflow files changed. 3. Confirmed `Claude PR Review` and `Cline PR Code Review` are both active in GitHub Actions after re-enabling Claude. How to verify on a real PR: 1. Open or update a non-draft PR. 2. Wait for both review workflows to run. 3. Check that one bot comment ends with: - `---` - `Generated by Claude PR Review` 4. Check that the other bot comment ends with: - `---` - `Generated by Cline PR Code Review` Potential breakage considered: - If prompt output format changes significantly, footer placement could vary. - If either workflow fails before posting a review, no footer will appear, which is expected and signals workflow failure rather than formatting regression. ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [x] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [x] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) Note on changeset checkbox: This is a non-user-facing workflow prompt change, so no changeset is required. ### Screenshots N/A. No UI changes. ### Additional Notes This is intentionally scoped to message clarity only. If you want harder guarantees later, we can follow up with workflow-level post-processing that appends a deterministic signature before publishing the final review comment. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds source-identifying footers to PR review comments in `claude-pr-review.yml` and `cline-pr-review.yml`. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds footer to comments in `claude-pr-review.yml` and `cline-pr-review.yml` to identify the source of the review comment. > - Footer for Claude: `---\nGenerated by Claude PR Review`. > - Footer for Cline: `---\nGenerated by Cline PR Code Review`. > - **Technical Approach**: > - Modifies prompt instructions in both workflow files to append the footer. > - No changes to triggers, permissions, or execution logic. > - **Testing**: > - Verified both workflow files contain new footer directives. > - Confirmed both workflows are active in GitHub Actions. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for ab15712903689da193799988b14bd9788feae153. pulls.title: fix(ui): add loading indicator and fix api_req_started rendering
pulls.body:
### Related Issue

Regression from #8264

### Description

The chat streaming UI refactor (#8264) removed the loading indicator that previously showed when an API request was in progress. This left users staring at a frozen UI during the ~500ms-1s latency between sending a message and receiving the first streamed content. The old `ErrorBlockTitle` component showed a spinning `ProgressIndicator` with "API Request..." text during this state, but the new `RequestStartRow` only renders content when tool activities, reasoning, or errors are present.

Additionally, `api_req_started` ChatRows now render as invisible padding since the refactor removed the old accordion UI (cost badge, expandable request payload). Reasoning messages already have their own standalone ChatRows, so these empty rows just waste vertical space throughout the conversation.

Changes:

1. "Thinking..." shimmer in Virtuoso Footer (`MessagesArea.tsx`) - Detects "waiting for response" state by checking if the last message in `modifiedMessages` is: empty (new task), `user_feedback` (follow-up sent), or `api_req_started` with no cost (request in progress, nothing streamed yet). Uses `modifiedMessages` (same source as `groupedMessages`) rather than `clineMessages` from context so both the Footer and the item list update in the same React render cycle, preventing flicker. The Footer is the sole loading indicator - RequestStartRow does not duplicate it.

2. Filter out empty `api_req_started` rows (`messageUtils.ts`) - `api_req_started` messages are now filtered from the visible message list unless they contain error/cancel content. This removes invisible padding that accumulated throughout conversations. Reasoning content is unaffected since `say: "reasoning"` messages render as their own standalone ChatRows.

3. Consistent spacing via `footerActive` flag (`MessageRenderer.tsx`) - Threads `isWaitingForResponse` from `MessagesArea` through the renderer so the last message skips `pb-2.5` bottom padding when the Footer is active, since the Footer provides its own `pt-2` top padding. Without this, there was double spacing between the last message and the indicator.

### Test Procedure

- Start a new task and verify "Thinking..." shimmer appears immediately (no frozen UI during backend processing)
- Verify "Thinking..." transitions smoothly to streamed content (reasoning, tools, text) with no flicker
- Send a follow-up message mid-conversation and verify "Thinking..." appears during the wait
- Verify spacing between "Thinking..." and adjacent messages matches normal ChatRow spacing
- Verify error states still render (cancel a request, trigger an API error)
- Verify conversations don't have invisible padding gaps from empty `api_req_started` rows
- Verify reasoning "Thoughts" sections still appear as standalone collapsible rows

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`)
-   [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Screenshots

N/A - UI change best verified interactively

### Additional Notes

The `api_req_started` filtering is more aggressive than strictly needed for the loading indicator fix, but it cleans up dead weight from the refactor. Every completed `api_req_started` was rendering an empty `<div>` wrapped in a ChatRow with `pt-2.5 px-4` padding, adding invisible spacing throughout conversations.

pulls.title: javascript fix(cli): handle stdin redirection in CI environments
pulls.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** Fixes regression introduced in #9038 ### Description Fix CLI crashing in CI environments (like GitHub Actions) when stdin is redirected (e.g., `< /dev/null`). **Problem:** In CI environments, stdin is typically redirected from `/dev/null`, meaning `process.stdin.isTTY` is `false`. The CLI was: 1. Detecting this as "piped input" and trying to read from stdin 2. Erroring with `Empty input received from stdin` even when a prompt argument was provided This broke the `cline-pr-review.yml` workflow which runs: ```bash npx cline --yolo 'Your PR review prompt...' ``` **Solution:** 1. **Extract mode selection into testable utility** - Created `cli/src/utils/mode-selection.ts` with `selectOutputMode()` function that determines when to use plain text mode vs interactive Ink mode. 2. **Add comprehensive unit tests** - Added 17 test cases in `cli/src/utils/mode-selection.test.ts` covering all stdin/stdout/TTY scenarios. 3. **Check `stdinIsTTY` for plain text mode** - Now uses plain text mode when stdin is not a TTY, avoiding Ink's raw mode requirement which fails on non-TTY streams. 4. **Only error on empty stdin when no prompt provided** - Changed from `if (stdinInput === "")` to `if (stdinInput === "" && !prompt)`. This allows: - `echo "" | cline` → error (no content, no prompt) - `cline "prompt" < /dev/null` → OK (has prompt, ignore empty stdin) - `cat file | cline "explain"` → OK (has content AND prompt) ### Test Procedure **Unit tests (17 test cases):** ```bash cd cli && npm test -- --reporter=verbose src/utils/mode-selection.test.ts ``` Tests cover: - Yolo flag → plain text mode - JSON flag → plain text mode - Piped stdin → plain text mode - Stdin not TTY → plain text mode - Stdout not TTY → plain text mode - Interactive (both TTYs) → Ink mode - Reason codes for telemetry **Manual testing:** ```bash # Redirected stdin (CI scenario) - previously crashed cline "say hello" < /dev/null # ✅ Works # Empty piped stdin with prompt - previously errored echo "" | cline "say hello" # ✅ Works # Empty piped stdin without prompt - should error echo "" | cline # ✅ Errors as expected # Yolo mode cline --yolo "say hello" # ✅ Works # Redirected stdout cline "say hello" > output.txt # ✅ Works # Piped input with content echo "explain this" | cline # ✅ Works ``` Verified the exact error from failed CI runs (`Empty input received from stdin. Please provide content to process.`) matches what this fix addresses. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes Once this PR is merged and a new CLI version is published to npm, the `cline-pr-review.yml` workflow will work automatically.

pulls.title: Fixing Content Truncation issues with Large files
pulls.body: ### Description This PR adds content truncation (100KB limit) to prevent large files and MCP responses from overwhelming the conversation context. Without this limit, reading very large files or receiving huge MCP tool responses could "brick" conversations by consuming too much context. **Changes:** - Add `truncateContent()` utility in `src/shared/content-limits.ts` with a 100KB limit (~25,000 tokens) - Apply truncation to file reading in `extract-text.ts` (PDF, DOCX, IPYNB, XLSX, and plain text) - Apply truncation to MCP tool responses (`UseMcpToolHandler.ts`) and MCP resource access (`AccessMcpResourceHandler.ts`) - Update tool descriptions for `read_file`, `access_mcp_resource`, and `use_mcp_tool` to inform the model about truncation behavior - Truncation message guides users to use `search_files` or `grep/head/tail` for targeted reading of large files ### Test Procedure 1. Read a file larger than 100KB - verify it's truncated with a clear message 2. Call an MCP tool that returns a very large response - verify truncation applies 3. Normal files under 100KB should not be affected ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` - [x] I have reviewed contributor guidelines ### Pre-flight Checklist - [ ] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds content truncation utility to limit large file and MCP response sizes to 400KB, applied in file reading and MCP handlers. > > - **Behavior**: > - Introduces `truncateContent()` in `content-limits.ts` to limit content to 400KB (~100,000 tokens). > - Applies truncation to file reading in `extract-text.ts` for PDF, DOCX, IPYNB, XLSX, and plain text files. > - Applies truncation to MCP tool responses in `AccessMcpResourceHandler.ts` and `UseMcpToolHandler.ts`. > - **Documentation**: > - Updates tool descriptions to inform about truncation behavior. > - Guides users to use `search_files` or `grep/head/tail` for targeted reading of large files. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for a6061dc19a389a67afc6c2041e941ead0fa8a84a. pulls.title: fix: use vscode.env.openExternal for auth in remote environments
pulls.body: ## Summary Fixes #5109 The OAuth authentication flow was broken in VS Code Server and remote environments (SSH Remote, VS Code Web, etc.) because the code used the npm `open` package directly, which tries to launch a browser on the server itself (which has no display). ## Solution This change routes browser URL opening through VS Code's native `vscode.env.openExternal()` API via the HostBridge pattern, which properly forwards URLs to the user's local machine in remote environments. ## Changes - Added `openExternal` RPC to `proto/host/env.proto` - Created VS Code handler in `src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.ts` using `vscode.env.openExternal()` - Updated `src/utils/env.ts` to use `HostProvider.env.openExternal()` - Added `openExternal` to CLI `CliEnvServiceClient` (uses npm `open` package) - Added `openExternal` to CLI `ACPEnvServiceClient` (uses npm `open` package) ## How It Works | Environment | Behavior | |-------------|----------| | Local VS Code | Opens browser normally (same as before) | | VS Code Server/Remote SSH | Forwards URL to local machine → opens browser there | | VS Code Web | Opens in a new browser tab | | CLI/Standalone | Uses npm `open` package directly (unchanged) | ## Related Issues - #5394 - "Get Started for Free Button not work when using SSH Remote" - #2152 - "Cline cannot be signed in when using vscode web" - #7971 - "Remote MCP Auth button doesn't work in VS Code remote desktop" ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes OAuth authentication in remote VS Code environments by using `vscode.env.openExternal()` to open URLs on the user's local machine. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes OAuth authentication in remote environments by using `vscode.env.openExternal()` instead of npm `open`. > - Handles URL opening in `openExternal()` in `src/utils/env.ts` and `src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.ts`. > - **RPC and Protobuf**: > - Adds `openExternal` RPC to `proto/host/env.proto`. > - **Client Implementations**: > - Updates `ACPEnvServiceClient` in `ACPHostBridgeClientProvider.ts` to use `openUrlInBrowser()`. > - Updates `CliEnvServiceClient` in `index.ts` to dynamically import and use `open` package. > - **Utilities**: > - Adds `openUrlInBrowser()` in `browser.ts` to handle URL opening using the `open` package. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 98250c67866efc806d4c797e341970e1f8d9175b. Non-unique keys may cause children to be duplicated and/or omitted — the behavior is unsupported and could change in a future version. ``` Note that [the Linear task](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-1268/hooks-bug-duplicate-react-child-key-error-after-provider-switch) has a good visual of what the broken behavior looks like. pulls.title: fix(cli): prevent hang when spawned without TTY
pulls.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** N/A (bug fix discovered during smoke test development) ### Description When the CLI is spawned as a child process without a TTY (e.g., from `spawn()` in smoke tests or CI environments), `process.stdin.isTTY` is `false` even when nothing is actually piped to stdin. This caused `readStdinIfPiped()` to wait up to 5 minutes for input that would never arrive, making the CLI hang. The fix uses `fs.fstatSync(0)` to check if stdin is actually a FIFO (pipe) or regular file before waiting for input. This correctly handles: - Spawned processes without TTY → returns immediately (no hang) - Actual piped input (`echo "x" | cline`) → waits and reads correctly - stdin from `/dev/null` → returns immediately ### Test Procedure Tested the following scenarios: 1. **Spawned without TTY** (the bug case): ```bash node cli/dist/cli.mjs --config "$TEST_DIR" -y "Say hello" # Before: hangs for 5 minutes # After: executes immediately ``` 2. **Piped input still works**: ```bash echo "What is 2+2?" | cline -y # Works correctly - reads piped input ``` 3. **Empty piped input**: ```bash echo "" | cline -y # Errors correctly with "Empty input received from stdin" ``` 4. **stdin from /dev/null**: ```bash cline -y "Say hello" < /dev/null # Works correctly - no hang ``` 5. **Smoke tests pass**: ```bash npx tsx evals/smoke-tests/run-smoke-tests.ts --trials 1 --scenario 01-create-file # PASS - 100% pass rate ``` ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots N/A - backend fix with no UI changes. ### Additional Notes This fix is critical for CLI usage in CI/CD environments and automated testing scenarios where the CLI is spawned as a subprocess without a TTY attached. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes CLI hang when spawned without TTY by checking stdin type with `fs.fstatSync(0)` in `readStdinIfPiped()` and adds comprehensive tests. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes CLI hang when spawned without TTY by checking if stdin is a FIFO or regular file using `fs.fstatSync(0)` in `readStdinIfPiped()`. > - Handles cases: spawned without TTY, actual piped input, stdin from `/dev/null`. > - **Tests**: > - Adds tests in `piped.test.ts` for TTY detection, stdin type detection, piped input scenarios, error handling, and real-world use cases. > - Mocks `fs.fstatSync` to simulate different stdin types. > - **Misc**: > - Adds changeset file `cli-stdin-hang.md` for patch release. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for a7b453f98a13b51f0190afa1edd3da49bc617292.
